If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3–5 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

In mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending downward, shift forecast downward by 1–2% to align with momentum.

In late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is positive but price is declining, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to reflect sentiment divergence.

If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, adjust forecast to rise by 1–2% in the next 5 days to capture sentiment momentum.

If sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon to avoid overcorrection from sentiment bias.
